hints: At constant speed on a horizontal road, driving force equals the total resistance: $F_D = 400 + 250 = 650\text{ N}$.
Use $P = F_D v$ with $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find power in W or kW.
walkthrough:
Calculate total resistance on the horizontal road:
$$R_{\text{total}} = 400 + 250 = 650\text{ N}$$

Since speed is constant, driving force $F_D = 650\text{ N}$. Compute engine power:
$$P = F_D v = 650 \times 25 = 16250\text{ W} = 16.25\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
At constant speed on a level road, acceleration is zero, so the engine driving force must exactly balance the total opposing resistance:
$$F_D = R_{\text{car}} + R_{\text{caravan}} = 400 + 250 = 650\text{ N}$$

State the power formula:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute $F_D = 650\text{ N}$ and constant velocity $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 650 \times 25 = 16250\text{ W}$$

Convert to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$:
$$P = \frac{16250}{1000} = 16.25\text{ kW}$$

hints: Calculate the new driving force from the increased power: $F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{39000}{25}$.
Apply Newton's second law to the whole system: $F_D - 650 = (1600 + 800)a$ to find acceleration $a$.
Apply Newton's second law to the caravan: $T - 250 = 800a$ to find the tension $T$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the new driving force at speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with $P = 39\text{ kW} = 39000\text{ W}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{39000}{25} = 1560\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the entire system ($m_{\text{total}} = 2400\text{ kg}$):
$$F_D - R_{\text{total}} = m_{\text{total}} a$$
$$1560 - 650 = 2400a$$
$$910 = 2400a$$
$$a = \frac{910}{2400} = \frac{91}{240} \approx 0.379\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally to the caravan ($800\text{ kg}$) to find tension $T$:
$$T - 250 = 800a$$
$$T - 250 = 800\left(\frac{91}{240}\right) = \frac{910}{3} \approx 303.33$$
$$T = 250 + 303.33 = 553.33 \approx 553\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Connected-Particle Systems: Calculates $F_D = 1560\text{ N}$, solves $1560 - 650 = 2400a$ for $a = 0.379\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and finds $T = 553\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
First, determine the new forward driving force from the sudden power increase to $P = 39000\text{ W}$ at instantaneous speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{39000}{25} = 1560\text{ N}$$

Next, treat the car and caravan as a single connected system of total mass $M = 1600 + 800 = 2400\text{ kg}$. The internal tension cancels out. Apply Newton's second law:
$$F_{\text{net}} = M a$$
$$F_D - R_{\text{total}} = M a$$
$$1560 - 650 = 2400a$$
$$910 = 2400a$$
Divide by $2400$:
$$a = \frac{910}{2400} = \frac{91}{240} \approx 0.379167 \approx 0.379\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Finally, isolate the caravan of mass $m = 800\text{ kg}$ to determine the tension $T$ in the tow-bar:
$$T - R_{\text{caravan}} = m a$$
$$T - 250 = 800 \times \frac{91}{240}$$
$$T - 250 = \frac{910}{3} \approx 303.33$$
Add $250$ to both sides:
$$T = 250 + 303.33 = 553.33 \approx 553\text{ N}$$

hints: At constant speed up the hill, driving force balances the total resistance plus the component of weight down the slope.
Calculate the component of total weight down the slope: $(1600 + 800)g \times 0.05$.
Find driving force $F_D = 650 + 1200 = 1850\text{ N}$, and use $P = F_D v$ with $P = 32.5\text{ kW} = 32500\text{ W}$ to solve for $v$.
walkthrough:
Calculate total opposing force at constant speed up the incline with $\sin\alpha = 0.05$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$F_{\text{opposing}} = R_{\text{total}} + M_{\text{total}} g\sin\alpha$$
$$F_D = 650 + (1600 + 800)(10)(0.05) = 650 + 24000(0.05) = 650 + 1200 = 1850\text{ N}$$

Use the power formula $P = F_D v$ with $P = 32.5\text{ kW} = 32500\text{ W}$:
$$32500 = 1850 v$$
$$v = \frac{32500}{1850} = \frac{650}{37} \approx 17.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Finds $F_D = 650 + 1200 = 1850\text{ N}$ and solves $32500 = 1850v$ to obtain $v = 17.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (or $650/37\text{ m s}^{-1}$).

teacher_walkthrough: For motion up the inclined hill at constant speed $v$, the acceleration is zero. The driving force $F_D$ must balance both the total resistances and the component of weight acting down the incline:

2. Component of weight down the hill for the combined car-caravan mass $M = 1600 + 800 = 2400\text{ kg}$:
$$W_{\parallel} = M g\sin\alpha = 2400 \times 10 \times 0.05 = 1200\text{ N}$$

Sum the resisting forces to find the driving force:
$$F_D = R_{\text{total}} + W_{\parallel} = 650 + 1200 = 1850\text{ N}$$

State the power equation:
$$P = F_D \times v \implies v = \frac{P}{F_D}$$

Substitute power $P = 32.5\text{ kW} = 32500\text{ W}$ and driving force $F_D = 1850\text{ N}$:
$$v = \frac{32500}{1850} = \frac{650}{37} \approx 17.5676 \approx 17.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
